aism_behavior: class-driven (no AISM counterpart -- AISM's argument.py has no signature vocabulary, no convention profile, and no regime reasoning of any kind).
notes: POSET keys, and why the profile needs them (codex Tier A review of the profile draft, finding 12): `reduction` is genuinely NOT totally ordered. `quasi-poly` is a time bound and `turing` is a query-model widening; neither implies the other. Linearising them into a chain would make one silently discharge the other -- quiet over-acceptance on a validity surface, which is the failure class this whole check exists to close. Here the context declares `quasi-poly` and the dependency needs `turing`: INCOMPARABLE, therefore NOT entailed. The symmetric direction (a turing context, a quasi-poly requirement) is equally refused and is pinned in test/gates/signature-entail.test.ts; both share this one reachability rule, so one fixture plus the unit test covers the pair. `karp`, the poset's bottom, does entail everything above it.
